active_problems.canonical_en: Postoperative left knee pain and limited range of motion
Anticoagulation duration for pre-existing right calf thrombosis requires verification
Ongoing postoperative fall and VTE-related risk management is needed

blockers.canonical_en: Before discharge, the clinical team should verify the indication, dose, and duration of anticoagulation for the pre-existing right calf thrombosis and document follow-up.

critical_facts_to_retain.canonical_en: The surgical side is the left knee, and the thrombosis side is the right lower leg; laterality must remain distinguished.
Right calf intermuscular vein thrombosis was present preoperatively.
Left total knee arthroplasty has been completed, with good prosthesis position on imaging.
The current record is favorable for discharge, but the specific anticoagulation course of rivaroxaban still needs to be verified.
Postoperative anemia and limited left-knee activity still require follow-up and rehabilitation management.

diagnoses.canonical_en: Pre-existing intermuscular venous thrombosis of the right calf

facts_to_retract_or_correct.canonical_en: The preoperative thrombus in the right calf must not be written as a left-sided thrombus, a new postoperative thrombus, or a prosthesis-related thrombus.
A record of rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily must not be interpreted as confirmation of a complete thrombosis-treatment course.
Do not claim evidence of long-term function, long-term efficacy, or complete disappearance of thrombosis.

management_state.canonical_en: Stable postoperative recovery and entry into the discharge and continuity-of-care stage; the current stable status cannot be interpreted as disappearance of thrombotic risk or rehabilitation needs.

required_delta_from_previous_checkpoint.canonical_en: New discharge medication evidence documents rivaroxaban 10 mg once daily, while the specific treatment duration for the pre-existing right calf thrombosis remains to be verified.
The patient has progressed from postoperative inpatient management to discharge preparation and continuity planning, with anticoagulation verification as a key continuity issue.

resolved_problems.canonical_en: The indication and preoperative decision for left knee arthroplasty are no longer unresolved
Definitive surgery is completed with no serious intraoperative complication documented

treatment_readiness.canonical_en: Left total knee replacement has been completed; postoperative incision, distal neurovascular status, and vital-sign records are stable, providing a basis for discharge readiness; however, verification of the anticoagulation course and continuity of rehabilitation still need to be completed.

hard_failure_rules_en: Do not confuse the surgical side, left knee, with the thrombosis side, right calf.
It must not be asserted that the right calf thrombosis has been adequately treated without verifying the treatment course.
Do not interpret the current discharge-preparation record as the absence of VTE, bleeding, anemia, infection, or fall risk.
Long-term efficacy, thrombus disappearance, or complete functional recovery must not be claimed based on undisclosed results.
critical_omission_rules_en: Failure to verify the existing right lower-leg venous thrombosis and anticoagulation course is a critical safety omission.
Omission of postoperative rehabilitation and fall prevention is an important continuity-of-care omission.
Omission of follow-up for postoperative anemia and warnings for abnormal symptoms is an important safety omission.
preliminary_risk_triggers_en: The anticoagulation course for existing right lower-leg venous thrombosis is unclear.
Postoperative status of the left knee is stable but rehabilitation and follow-up are still needed

stopping.rationale_en: The available evidence shows stable vital signs, a dry incision without redness or swelling, intact limb neurovascular status, and a well-positioned left knee prosthesis; the record meets documented discharge-readiness criteria. Discharge with continuity follow-up is therefore reasonable rather than continued inpatient investigation of all issues. Management must not stop completely: the anticoagulation duration for the pre-existing right calf thrombosis requires clinical verification, and postoperative anemia, limited knee motion, and fall risk require ongoing follow-up.
remaining_blockers_en: Before discharge, verify the anticoagulation indication, rivaroxaban dose, and specific course for the pre-existing right calf venous thrombosis.
Complete continuity confirmation for discharge medications, rehabilitation, fall prevention, and follow-up arrangements.

public_context.admission_diagnosis: Degenerative lesion of the left knee

question.question_en: At this time point, use only available evidence to identify key evidence, supported claims, patient state, appropriate next actions, and whether stopping or follow-up is safe.
